inputs.prompt: Requested framing: Over shoulder. Edit the reference photograph into a new camera shot of the SAME scene. Preserve the exact same person and facial identity, hair, outfit, bag, object design, materials, lighting and set architecture from the reference. Change camera position and framing as requested; do not simply repeat the reference composition. OVER THE LEFT SHOULDER: camera immediately behind the reference woman with the exact same rounded face, lowered eyes, light chestnut chin-length bob with soft waves curling outward at the ends and right side part, mustard yellow canvas coat with metal buttons, shoulder tabs and flap chest pockets, rich teal cable-knit scarf, her left shoulder and back of head clearly visible occupying the LEFT THIRD foreground. Look past her shoulder toward her two hands holding the exact compass in the reference: a deep cylindrical brass case with a slightly flared base, side wall height about 40 percent of dial diameter; plain brass lid with two interior rivets hinged at upper left; a completely plain unmarked cream dial with NO tick marks, NO lines, NO numerals and NO letters; four broad pointed grey-blue triangular arms making an X, with a SMALL smooth flat muted-pink circular pivot with NO engraving or rings; no ring or bail, no chain, no compass rose, only one compass over the same wooden bench. Camera is slightly above hands so the cream dial, X needle and thick case side wall are clearly visible. Keep the teal scarf visibly teal (not navy or black), same knit weave, same bob hair texture and warm chestnut colour. Keep the mustard coat canvas and seams, no additional bracelet, bag, object or person. The scarf must show raised twisted cable-knit all around the back and side of her neck, not a smooth band or straight simple ribbing. Offset camera to her left enough to show her left cheek in profile and the side of the cable-knit scarf.. Keep only elements visible in this framing; do not force a face into a detail or rear view.
